headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error: Semantic Kernel can read/write files and call MCP/OpenAPI tools, while PaddleOCR processes documents/images and can emit raw extracted content into the orchestration flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A plausible injection path exists because Semantic Kernel can use MCP/OpenAPI tools and read/write files, while PaddleOCR processes document/image content that may be attacker-controlled. If PaddleOCR output is fed into SK prompts or plugins without sanitization, raw document text can steer tool use. This is not provably blocked by either profile.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is inserted into Semantic Kernel prompts or plugin inputs without escaping
IF an MCP server or OpenAPI tool consumes document text as instructions
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter/template around OCR text before passing it onward
Strip tool-like markers from OCR output in under 5 minutes
Disable MCP tools for the OCR-to-agent path
requires-engineering: add provenance tags and instruction/data separation
requires-engineering: add prompt-injection regression tests

B_data_leakage.rationale: Semantic Kernel can read and write filesystem data and send context to broad networked model providers, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images. If both operate on the same workspace, sensitive document contents can flow from A into B and then to third-party APIs. The profiles do not show isolation or redaction by default.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or application-defined workspace
IF OCR outputs contain sensitive document text and are forwarded into SK context or plugins
mitigations: Separate workspaces for OCR input and orchestration output
Redact sensitive fields before handing text to Semantic Kernel
Restrict SK network egress to approved endpoints only
Turn off file ingestion for the SK path when handling sensitive docs
requires-engineering: add per-document access controls and audit logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: PaddleOCR can process documents while Semantic Kernel can write files and coordinate plugins over shared application-defined files. Even without shell access, overlapping write/read on the same workspace can cause races, overwritten artifacts, or inconsistent intermediate outputs. The profiles do not show locking or coordination primitives.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or application-defined file set
IF multiple Semantic Kernel instances share the same memory store or workspace
mitigations: Assign separate output directories per agent
Use unique filenames per run
Pause concurrent writes during OCR export
Add a simple lock file or mutex in the orchestrator
requires-engineering: implement transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is designed to act on plugin/tool outputs, and PaddleOCR produces extracted text that may be treated as authoritative downstream. If SK consumes OCR results without verification, OCR mistakes or adversarial text can cascade into incorrect actions, commits, or API calls. This is a default-path risk because the library is built for agent/tool chaining.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is used as direct input to Semantic Kernel tool calls or agent decisions
IF SK executes actions based on OCR-derived facts without a verification step
mitigations: Insert a human review step for OCR-derived facts
Require confidence thresholds before actioning OCR text
Compare OCR output against source documents for critical fields
Disable auto-execution on first-pass OCR results
requires-engineering: add structured validation and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: PaddleOCR touches documents and images, while Semantic Kernel can route those contents to broad third-party model providers and plugins. If the documents include regulated data, the pair can create residency or retention mismatches because SK handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials but no explicit compliance controls are shown. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their interaction.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through PaddleOCR and then forwarded by Semantic Kernel to external model providers
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the document class
mitigations: Block regulated data from the SK path
Use a provider with an approved residency region
Set short retention on intermediate OCR artifacts
Document the data flow for the specific document class
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
